summary: First test run for the new /the-apartments-tac.html page. Executed 11 review-request checks via Playwright at multiple viewports (375/390/430/768/1024/1440). Result: page loads cleanly with zero console errors, zero horizontal overflow at every tested width, hero/intro/action-bar/floor-plan/map/form/nearby/east-west-regression/link-check all pass. Two minor observations reported to main agent, both non-blocking.

ui_bugs.issue: At the exact instant #tacPlansLightbox gains .is-open the close button reports getBoundingClientRect w=0,h=0 (top=0,left=0) and Playwright refuses to click it with 'Element is not visible'. DOM .click() and keyboard Escape both dismiss the lightbox correctly and the button IS visually rendered in the top-right of the lightbox in a screenshot, so this looks like a transient layout/animation timing where the button briefly has no measured box. Users clicking with a real mouse are unlikely to hit that window, but it caused an automated test failure. Recommend ensuring the button has an explicit width/height (or removing the entering animation from the close button) so it always has a non-zero bounding rect once .is-open is applied.

integration_issues.issue: During one Playwright run the request for /media/video/tac/tac-construction.webm was recorded as failed, but a direct curl to the same URL returns HTTP 200 with 5.16 MB of body and the <video> element ends up with readyState=4 and paused=false. This looks like a Playwright request-abort artifact when the page navigates during preload, not a real broken asset. Just flagging so main agent doesn't chase it.
